sentences.text: Intiornis was a tiny bird with a body length of around 15 cm, roughly the size of a sparrow.
Its limbs featured three primary toes that were nearly the same length.
Intiornis represents the smallest known enantiornithes from South America.
The animal is known from a partial hind limb discovered in the Las Curtiembres Formation.
Fernando Emilio Novas, Federico Lisandro Agnolín, and Carlos Agustín Scanferla named the genus in 2010, establishing Intiornis inexpectatus as the type species.
Researchers suggest that Intiornis's long, equal-length toes and large curved claws indicate an adaptation for perching.
Intiornis belongs to the family Avisauridae and is a member of the subclass Enantiornithes. It is a monotypic genus known only from the species I. inexpectatus.
Intiornis lived between 83.6 and 72.2 million years ago during the Campanian stage.
